sections.title: Habitat and form
sections.text: Common sea-lavender is a glabrous perennial of European Atlantic salt meadows that are periodically flooded. It is usually 20–50 cm tall and flowers in summer.

sections.title: Leaves and flowers
sections.text: The leaves form a basal rosette. Leaf glands excrete salt. Small violet flowers are grouped in compact spikelets on branched panicles.

sections.title: Edibility
sections.text: No reliable food use was included for this species. The Dutch common name lamsoor can be confused with Tripolium pannonicum, a different salt-marsh plant eaten as a vegetable.
